# a1ui

> A collection of React components and blocks inspired by designs found online, installed as editable source through the shadcn CLI.

## Supported projects

The supported baseline is React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS 4. Installation and the published examples are verified in a clean Next.js App Router project. Vite and other React frameworks may work but are not covered by that verification. Check their configuration before proceeding. These are client components; retain their "use client" directives. Parent components with state or callback props also need a client boundary in a React Server Components app.

## Choose and install

1. Inspect the user's request, package.json, lockfile, components.json, import aliases, and global CSS in the target project. Work in the app or workspace that owns components.json. Do not silently change frameworks or upgrade an incompatible project.
2. Read the [registry catalog](http://localhost:3000/r/registry.json). Match descriptions, categories, and meta.a1ui.useCases to the request. Check meta.a1ui.limitations and requirements. If nothing fits, explain the gap instead of installing an unrelated block.
3. Read the chosen block's Markdown guide below. It includes actual imports, props, examples, and dependencies. Read the registry item's embedded source when needed.
4. If components.json is missing in an otherwise compatible project, initialize shadcn using the project's package runner and the existing framework and theme. Inspect `shadcn init --help` for current options. Preserve existing styles. Do not force initialization over an existing configuration.
5. Inspect any existing destination files. Use `shadcn add <item-url> --dry-run` and `--diff` before updating them. Reuse existing compatible components or merge deliberately. Never use `--overwrite` automatically.
6. Install from the selected item's URL using the target project's package manager. Replace NAME with the exact catalog name:

```text
npm: npx shadcn@latest add http://localhost:3000/r/NAME.json --yes
pnpm: pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add http://localhost:3000/r/NAME.json --yes
yarn: yarn dlx shadcn@latest add http://localhost:3000/r/NAME.json --yes
bun: bunx --bun shadcn@latest add http://localhost:3000/r/NAME.json --yes
```

7. Adapt the documented example to the requested page. Use the target project's actual import aliases, state, data, and callbacks. Keep accessible labels and reduced-motion behavior. Preserve the app's theme; check the guide for CSS tokens or font requirements. Demo artwork is not included.
8. Run the project's typecheck, lint, and build scripts where available. Render the result, check browser errors and styling, and exercise the primary interaction. Report the selected block, changed files, checks, and any missing integration data.

## Components and blocks

- [Accordion](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/accordion.md): An accordion whose panels glide open to their natural height, stagger their content in, and turn a chevron or fold a plus into a minus. FAQs, settings sections, and long forms where readers open one or several sections at a time.
- [Alert Dialog](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/alert-dialog.md): A confirmation dialog that springs in, shakes when you click outside it, and fades out before it unmounts. Confirming destructive or irreversible actions such as deleting a project, signing out, or discarding unsaved changes.
- [Arc Reel](http://localhost:3000/docs/blocks/arc-reel.md): An infinitely looping reel with curved provider cards and synchronized scroll controls. Looping galleries, provider cards, or logo reels with drag and keyboard controls.
- [ASCII Lens](http://localhost:3000/docs/blocks/ascii-lens.md): An image rendered as ASCII, with a circular lens that reveals the original. Portfolio and product cards that reveal source artwork through an interactive lens.
- [ASCII Morph](http://localhost:3000/docs/blocks/ascii-morph.md): A cloud of characters that morphs into a globe, a flower, and an A1 monogram. Interactive ASCII illustrations for landing pages, portfolios, and identity studies.
- [ASCII Terrain](http://localhost:3000/docs/blocks/ascii-terrain.md): A landscape made of characters, with rolling hills, pointer sculpting, and click ripples. Interactive ASCII landscapes and decorative hero backgrounds.
- [Checkbox](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/checkbox.md): A checkbox that draws its check, morphs from an indeterminate dash, and can strike through its label. Task lists, consent fields, and select-all groups where a parent shows a partial selection.
- [Compare Curtain](http://localhost:3000/docs/blocks/compare-curtain.md): A draggable divider that reveals two aligned images or design states. Before-and-after images, design revisions, and visual product comparisons.
- [Confirm Button](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/confirm-button.md): A hold-to-confirm button with a directional color fill and configurable hold duration. Deliberate confirmation actions that require an uninterrupted pointer or keyboard hold.
- [Confirmation Button](http://localhost:3000/docs/blocks/confirmation-button.md): A drag-to-confirm button with a dotted arrow, pending feedback, and a confirmed state. Deliberate confirmation actions with drag, keyboard, and asynchronous feedback.
- [Copy Button](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/copy-button.md): A copy button that animates its icon and label into a checkmark and copied confirmation. Copying text, links, and code with animated success feedback.
- [Dialog](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/dialog.md): A modal dialog that grows out of the button that opened it and shrinks back into it, over a blurred backdrop. Focused tasks that interrupt the page, such as editing a profile, sharing a link, or confirming settings, where the dialog should feel connected to the button that opened it.
- [Drawer](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/drawer.md): A bottom or side sheet that springs in, follows your drag, rubber-bands, and can scale the page behind it. Mobile-first forms, pickers, share sheets, and filter panels that slide up from the bottom or in from the right and dismiss with a drag.
- [Dropdown Menu](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/dropdown-menu.md): A shadcn dropdown with open and close transitions and a traveling highlight. Action menus with animated open and close transitions and a shared pointer and keyboard highlight.
- [Hover Card](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/hover-card.md): A link preview card that springs out from its trigger and staggers its contents in. Profile mentions, linked repositories, and glossary terms that preview more detail without leaving the page.
- [Icon Toggle](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/icon-toggle.md): A two-state icon button that morphs its SVG paths on every click. Icon toggles with a reversible morph between two states, such as menu and close or play and pause.
- [Integration Hub](http://localhost:3000/docs/blocks/integration-hub.md): A connected workspace with six tools and animated pulses flowing into a central product. Product integration diagrams with up to six tools, inward pulses, and optional tool selection.
- [Loading Button](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/loading-button.md): A loading button with animated icon and label transitions for async actions and network requests. Submitting data, saving changes, and running network requests with loading, success, and retry feedback.
- [Menu](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/menu.md): A shared highlight that travels between focused and selected menu items. Sidebar navigation and view selectors with a traveling focus and selection highlight.
- [OTP Input](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/otp-input.md): A one-time code field with 4, 6, or 8 slots, a traveling focus highlight, and characters that rise into place. Entering numeric or alphanumeric verification, two-factor, and invite codes of 4, 6, or 8 characters.
- [Particle Menu](http://localhost:3000/docs/blocks/particle-menu.md): Grainy symbols that scatter around your pointer and spring back into place. Artistic navigation with interactive particle symbols.
- [Password Input](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/password-input.md): A password field that requires a strong password, with a strength meter that opens its requirements on hover, and a show/hide toggle. Requiring a strong password in sign-up, password reset, and change-password forms, with a compact meter that reveals each requirement on hover.
- [Peel Stack](http://localhost:3000/docs/blocks/peel-stack.md): A layered paper stack that rotates through collections with buttons, arrow keys, or a swipe. Layered collections, portfolio studies, and attachment cards with manual navigation.
- [Popover](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/popover.md): A popover that springs out of its trigger, or morphs the trigger button itself into the panel. Small anchored panels such as display settings, filters, or share options, and a feedback button that opens into a short form in place.
- [Progress](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/progress.md): A progress bar, ring, or step row whose fill springs to each value while the percentage rolls like a counter. Uploads, onboarding checklists, quotas, and background jobs where a value changes over time or is not yet known.
- [Radio Group](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/radio-group.md): A radio group whose single dot slides from option to option, with a card variant whose highlighted border glides between cards. Plan pickers, settings with a few mutually exclusive choices, and shipping or payment options shown as cards.
- [Section Rail](http://localhost:3000/docs/blocks/section-rail.md): A compact reading rail that tracks progress through page sections. Table of contents and reading progress for long pages with sections.
- [Shape Flow](http://localhost:3000/docs/blocks/shape-flow.md): Text that reflows around a floating ASCII duck, powered by Pretext. Editorial text wrapping around a floating ASCII duck.
- [Slider](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/slider.md): A slider with magnetic stops that catch the thumb and pulse as you slide through them. Adjusting values with magnetic catches at meaningful presets or unevenly spaced stops.
- [Spiral Text](http://localhost:3000/docs/blocks/spiral-text.md): Text set on a responsive spiral that tightens under pressure and ripples on release. Decorative spiral typography with pointer interaction.
- [Switch](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/switch.md): A switch whose thumb squashes on press, springs across the track, and can rotate icons in and out. Settings that apply immediately, such as notifications or dark mode, with optional icons for the two states.
- [Tabs](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/tabs.md): Tabs with a spring indicator that slides between triggers, a hover highlight, and direction-aware panels. Switching between related views, such as dashboard sections or settings panes, where the active tab should feel connected to the last one.
- [Tag Input](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/tag-input.md): A text field that collects multiple tags, with a two-step Backspace removal and an optional limit. Collecting keywords, topics, skills, labels, or email recipients as a list of short tags in forms.
- [Text Banner](http://localhost:3000/docs/blocks/text-banner.md): Bold text and staggered pixel separators in a seamless, infinitely scrolling banner. Continuously scrolling words or phrases with separators for page banners.
- [Text Scramble](http://localhost:3000/docs/blocks/text-scramble.md): Reveals new text from left to right through a scramble of random characters. Animating changing headings, labels, or status text through scrambled characters.
- [Toast](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/toast.md): Toasts that stack as a deck, fan out on hover, and swipe away, with a loading state that morphs into success. Save confirmations, errors, undo actions, and long-running uploads or deploys that resolve to success or failure.
- [Toggle Group](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/toggle-group.md): A segmented control whose surface slides between items, or chips that pop in with a check when pressed. Switching a view or alignment with a segmented control, or picking several filters as chips.
- [Tooltip](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/tooltip.md): A tooltip that springs from its trigger and glides between neighboring triggers, morphing its size and text. Icon-button toolbars, editor controls, and dense action bars where hints should follow the pointer from button to button.
- [Validated Input](http://localhost:3000/docs/components/validated-input.md): A labeled text field that checks its value against a Zod schema and animates the error and success states. Validating emails, usernames, URLs, and other single-line text fields with Zod in native forms.

## Optional shadcn MCP setup

Direct URL installation works without MCP. For agents that already use the shadcn MCP server, merge this entry into the target project's components.json registries object, preserving existing entries:

```json
{
  "registries": {
    "@a1ui": "http://localhost:3000/r/{name}.json"
  }
}
```

The [registry index](http://localhost:3000/r/registry.json) supports shadcn discovery. With this configuration, use `shadcn search @a1ui -q "reading progress"`, `shadcn view @a1ui/section-rail`, or `shadcn add @a1ui/section-rail --yes` through the project's package runner. See the [shadcn MCP setup guide](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/registry/mcp) for client configuration.
